acv.quote: It would have been about seventy-five K a year.

header.reason: The CFO froze all new vendor projects after a missed Q3, with paper sent but unsigned. Renee calls it timing, but Owen had asked for a payback 'number that's ours' a month earlier, it was never built, and finance still saw the project as a 'nice to have'.

findings.label: What started it
findings.finding: Aim messaging at product leaders whose pricing changes or new tiers are stuck behind a homegrown billing system nobody owns anymore.
findings.quote: The billing system is homegrown, built by a guy who left, and every pricing change takes them a quarter.

findings.label: Who decided
findings.finding: Get the CFO into the cycle before paper goes out, with a payback session built on the customer's own engineering time, billing errors and lapsed subscriptions.
findings.quote: I can't get this past Diane without a number that's ours.

findings.label: The competitor
findings.finding: Build a do-nothing objection talk track that makes failed-card lapses nobody chases look 'on fire' to finance, and confirm with Owen no other vendor was considered.
findings.quote: if it isn't on fire, it isn't funded.

findings.label: Our message
findings.finding: Lead with the price-change, trials and proration demo, and stop pitching billing as revenue growth to product buyers.
findings.quote: we're not trying to grow revenue with billing, we're trying to stop it being a tax on the roadmap.

findings.label: Missing proof
findings.finding: Build a migration reference customer who moved subscriptions in stages without re-collecting card details, ready for champions to call.
findings.quote: He wanted to talk to someone who'd done it.

findings.label: Their words
findings.finding: Use 'a tax on the roadmap' and 'a quarter of roadmap in five minutes' in product-buyer messaging instead of revenue language.
findings.quote: that's a quarter of roadmap in five minutes.
